competitors.name: OpenBeds (Bamboo Health, formerly Appriss Health)
competitors.what_they_do: Incumbent closed-loop behavioral health bed registry and referral network. Shows real-time availability, has inclusion/exclusion criteria for decision support, tracks accept/decline with reasons, replaces calls and faxes with digital referrals. Used by state and 988 systems (Delaware, North Carolina BH SCAN, Nevada, New Hampshire). Its rural-health-transformation messaging is aimed at the same funding stream. Data comes from facility self-reporting. No AI or voice calling found on the product page. Bamboo Bridge adds AI-enabled triage and human navigators for patient navigation (https://bamboohealth.com/press-release/bamboo-bridge-delivers-market-leading-behavioral-healthcare-navigation-improving-access-outcomes-and-system-efficiency/).
competitors.scale_or_funding: Acquired by Appriss Health in 2019 (Crunchbase: https://www.crunchbase.com/acquisition/appriss-health-acquires-openbeds--ea0ee1bf). Operates in 52 states and territories per its own site. Established vendor with state contracts. Contract values not found.

competitors.name: Behavioral Health Link (GCAL Real-Time Bed Registry and Crisis Now platform)
competitors.what_they_do: Georgia's crisis call line operator that sells a bed registry and referral platform. It suggests the closest facilities whose admission criteria match the caller's needs, supports business rules for inclusion and exclusion, and supports electronic referrals. Also staffs human crisis call centers that do placement work.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Established nonprofit and vendor with state government contracts (Georgia DBHDD and others). Funding not found.

competitors.name: State and hospital-association psychiatric bed registries (NC BH SCAN, WHA Psychiatric Bed Locator, Minnesota Bed Tracker, MABHA, Michigan registry dashboard)
competitors.what_they_do: Free or state-funded portals where facilities post open psychiatric beds. NC BH SCAN now has hourly automated bed availability, 112 facilities and more than 3,500 beds (about 80% of state capacity). Washington's tool tells users to still contact the facility to arrange transfer. Other examples: https://www.whainfocenter.com/provider-services/psychiatric-bed-locator and https://www.mha.org/newsroom/mdhhs-launches-michigan-psychiatric-bed-registry-dashboard/
competitors.scale_or_funding: Government or hospital-association funded, statewide. They mainly track bed counts, not tacit acceptance rules. They are the free substitute that any state buyer will compare against.

competitors.name: Human placement and crisis-access services (Illinois CARES Line, Massachusetts EPIA protocol, regional psychiatric emergency services, telepsychiatry vendors such as Array Behavioral Care and Access TeleCare)
competitors.what_they_do: State-run or vendor-run humans who do the calling and placement for EDs. The Illinois CARES Line screens and refers children in crisis. Massachusetts runs an expedited admissions policy with a bed search protocol (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/expedited-psychiatric-inpatient-admissions-epia-policy). Array (https://arraybc.com/partner-with-us/hospitals-and-health-systems/) and Access TeleCare (https://accesstelecare.com/specialties/behavioral-health/emergency-departments/) sell tele-behavioral health that reduces boarding without changing the placement process.
competitors.scale_or_funding: State-funded programs and venture-backed telehealth vendors. Not a software substitute, but they are where a state's placement budget already goes.

competitors.name: Transfer center platforms (TeleTracking TransferCenterIQ, Central Logic, RelateCare, Epic patient-flow center)
competitors.what_they_do: Software and outsourced staffing that let receiving health systems accept interfacility transfers for stroke, trauma, OB and cardiac. They sit on the receiving side and are Epic-integrated. They own the non-psychiatric transfer workflow that the idea lists as a use case. Also see https://relatecare.com/clinical-services/hospital-transfer-center/ and https://appsource.microsoft.com/en-us/product/web-apps/centrallogic.transfercenter?tab=overview
competitors.scale_or_funding: Large established vendors sold to health systems. Central Logic is well known in the market. Funding not verified.

competitors.name: Post-acute referral and placement platforms (Aidin, CarePort/WellSky, Ensocare)
competitors.what_they_do: Let facilities set referral criteria such as diagnosis exclusions, insurance, and acuity so hospitals send fitting referrals. WellSky/CarePort applies facility-specific clinical rules automatically (https://wellsky.com/wellsky-centralizes-post-acute-referral-intake-with-intelligent-ai-integration/). This is the same 'encode who accepts what' concept in a neighboring market. It shows the model works but is facility-maintained, and nobody has extended it to psychiatric units or rural ED transfers.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Established, widely deployed by hospitals. Aidin and WellSky are the incumbents in post-acute referral management.

competitors.name: Horizontal healthcare voice AI platforms (Assort Health, Infinitus, Hippocratic AI, Prosper AI, SuperDial, Retell)
competitors.what_they_do: Well-funded voice agents that make outbound calls (scheduling, referrals, payer calls, benefit verification, directory data verification). None advertise nightly calls to receiving facilities to extract acceptance rules, but any could add it, and the same tech powers this idea's 'off-the-shelf voice agent'. Directory-verification calling is the closest business model (https://www.hilabs.com/blog/ai-voice-agent-for-healthcare-provider-data-verification).
competitors.scale_or_funding: Assort Health $120M Series C at $1.2B valuation (June 2026); Prosper AI $30M (https://www.mobihealthnews.com/news/prosper-ai-secures-30m-scale-healthcare-voice-ai-agents); SuperDial $15M Series A (https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/ai-and-machine-learning/voice-ai-company-superdial-picks-15m-series-automate-insurance-calls).

white_space: Nobody found does the specific thing. Across roughly 20 searches, no startup, product, or open-source tool uses voice agents to phone receiving psychiatric units and specialty hospitals on a schedule and record their tacit acceptance rules, the name and hours of the decision-maker, and the script that works. The unserved wedge is real but narrow. (1) Registries (OpenBeds, BHL, state portals) capture bed counts and formal criteria through facility self-report. The 2019 ASPE and Psychiatric Services work found no state registry linked to EHR or ADT data, and respondents rated registry accuracy and timeliness poor. Only NC has hourly automation, and that is bed count, not rule extraction. (2) Nobody delivers a ranked call list plus script by SMS to a rural ER charge nurse. Registries are portals that still end in 'call the facility'. (3) The hardest-to-place groups are children, autism and IDD, aggression, medically complex, out-of-state Medicaid. Boarding research shows these patients wait longest, and generic registry filters handle them worst. (4) Decline reasons and real decision-makers are not aggregated across facilities anywhere. Not unserved: bed availability, digital referrals, and generic outbound voice AI. Also not a clean white space: stroke, trauma and OB, where hospital-run transfer centers and TeleTracking, Central Logic and RelateCare already own the workflow.
evidence_of_demand: Problem demand is strong. Payment demand for this specific product is unproven, and I found no RFP, vendor contract, or customer purchase for an acceptance-rule intelligence service. Evidence: (1) Boarding is a documented, costly crisis. Among about 1.4M national pediatric mental health ED visits ending in admission or transfer, 13.1% lasted 24 hours or more (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12159435/). Prolonged boarders were mostly declined by all state inpatient units (69%) and were more often under 12, on Medicaid or uninsured, or had neurodevelopmental disorders (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33279330). Only 38% of rural and remote EDs have designated transfer guidelines for children with mental health issues. A 14-year-old was boarded 42 days. NPR 2025: https://www.npr.org/sections/shots-health-news/2025/08/15/nx-s1-5502689/pediatric-mental-health-er-boarding-jama-health-forum. Interhospital transfer acceptance falls with boarding and census, especially in rural settings (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12120653/). (2) Registry limits are documented. ASPE/Psychiatric Services found manual updates, no EHR link, and 'poor' accuracy ratings (https://aspe.hhs.gov/sites/default/files/migrated_legacy_files/190716/IPBedTrack.pdf, https://psychiatryonline.org/doi/10.1176/appi.ps.201900079). The Washington locator says to still call the facility to arrange transfer. (3) Money is flowing. States buy registries. NC launched BH SCAN, Michigan a registry dashboard, Montana had a 2025 legislative item to adopt an electronic bed registry (https://www.dphhs.mt.gov/assets/2025Legislature/BHSFG-09-Adopt-ElectronicBedRegistryandEnhance.pdf, page returned 404 on my fetch so treat as unverified). RHTP is $50B over five years, about $10B per year, with state awards of $147M to $281M and up to 10% allowed for tech pilots (https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/press-releases/cms-announces-50-billion-awards-strengthen-rural-health-all-50-states; https://shvs.org/resources/may-2026-state-implementation-of-the-rural-health-transformation-program-ramps-up/). Kentucky's RHTP telebehavioral hub includes 'shared reporting and registry functions' (https://www.chfs.ky.gov/agencies/os/oas/Documents/RHT%20Telebehavioral%20Health%20Support%20-%20RFA.pdf). Behavioral health boarding, crisis, and tele-behavioral projects are funded in KY, NE, TN. (4) Comparable spend on a similar model exists. Aidin and CarePort get paid for facility-criteria-based referral matching in post-acute, and voice-AI directory verification is an emerging paid category. Caveats: RHTP money is going mostly to crisis facilities, tele-behavioral and workforce, and I saw no state line item for placement intelligence. Critics call RHTP funds a band-aid (https://lexingtonky.news/2026/08/31/critics-say-rural-health-transformation-program-funds-are-a-band-aid-that-comes/). The $300-600 per ER per month price is an unsupported assumption.
sharper_angle: Narrow it and re-position it as the verification layer under existing registries, not a rival registry. (1) Start with one hard, measurable slice: pediatric and IDD/autism psychiatric placement for rural EDs in a single state, where boarding days are already reported and Medicaid or the children's behavioral health agency feels the cost. Drop stroke, trauma and OB, which TeleTracking, Central Logic and RelateCare own. (2) Sell 'ground truth' rather than another portal. Run a nightly call program that measures actual acceptance behavior (accept and decline rates by population, real decision-maker, hours, working script) and sell it to state agencies and hospital associations as a QA and boarding-reduction service, and as a data feed or partner integration to OpenBeds, Behavioral Health Link and the state bed portals. Their weakness is self-reported data, so co-opt them instead of racing them. (3) Keep humans in the loop. Start with human or hybrid callers, because intake nurses may refuse to talk to bots or may not disclose exclusions to one, and the calls only cover facility rules with no patient data. Measure willingness to answer before building an SMS product. (4) Handle legal risk up front. Publishing explicit exclusions like 'no autism' invites ADA and Section 504 disputes and facility pushback. Show ER users a private acceptance-likelihood score, the decision-maker and the script, and keep raw exclusion text non-public. Use SMS only with de-identified, patient-free queries or move to a HIPAA-compliant channel. (5) Prove it before selling it. Use the founder-nurse binder as a seed and run a 60-80 facility pilot, with pre and post placement time and call counts at five ERs, before approaching RHTP offices. Fastest kill test: in the first two weeks, check that at least 60% of intake lines will give rule answers to a voice agent, and that a state buyer will name a budget line."
